title: Local-GS: An Order-Independent Gaussian Splatting Training Accelerator Exploiting Splat Locality
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting training on edge devices is bottlenecked by depth-wise data dependencies between overlapping Gaussians, limited memory, and hardware under-utilization. Order-dependent rendering requires sequential processing, preventing parallelism exploitation.
motivation: Gaussian Splatting has emerged as SOTA for 3D view synthesis with superior rendering quality; enabling on-demand training on resource-constrained edge devices would unlock applications in robotics, AR, and autonomous systems.
method: Local-GS uses order-independent rendering—a method that displays 3D objects made from overlapping Gaussians (mathematical shapes) without requiring front-to-back processing order. Normally, rendering order creates dependencies that force sequential processing, but removing this requirement allows nearby Gaussians to be processed in parallel. The same hardware cores simultaneously handle both rendering (drawing the image) and gradient propagation (the learning process), which makes efficient use of processors in resource-limited edge devices.
key_novelty: Local-GS is the first GPU accelerator for training Gaussian Splatting on edge devices, using order-independent rendering to enable parallel processing of nearby shapes.
contributions: Order-independent rendering breaking depth-wise dependencies between overlapping Gaussians
Parallel pixel intersection test unit for workload scheduling based on splat locality
Unified training-rendering cores for simultaneous gradient computation and rendering
26.9-53x training speedup vs. Jetson NX, three orders of magnitude efficiency boost

metrics.energy_efficiency: 3 orders of magnitude vs. edge GPU

primary_theme: Edge accelerator for Gaussian Splatting training with order-independent rendering
